screening_decisions.reason: This is a two-year maintenance RCT comparing monthly maintenance IPT vs supportive clinical management in remitted depressed elderly patients. Meets all criteria: elderly population, successfully treated/remitted from depression, randomized to maintenance treatment (psychological therapy).

This is a review/discussion article about psychotherapy for depression in older people, not an RCT. It mentions evidence from 'a limited number of randomised controlled trials' but is itself not a primary RCT.
This is a Cochrane review examining efficacy of antidepressant classes, not a primary RCT. The objectives state it is a review to examine efficacy across classes.
This is an observational population-based study examining antidepressant prescribing patterns in Lombardy, Italy. Not an RCT and does not involve randomization to treatment.

This is an RCT where 58 elderly subjects remitted from major depression received continuation nortriptyline for 16 weeks, then were randomly assigned to nortriptyline maintenance therapy or placebo for up to 2 years. Meets all criteria: elderly, remitted from depression, randomized to maintenance treatment.
This is a Cochrane review (indicated by cochranelibrary.com reference), not a primary RCT. It reviews evidence from RCTs but is not itself an RCT.

This is a community-based, prospective, observational study examining the relationship between depressive symptoms and functional disability. Not an RCT and does not involve randomization to treatment.
This is a systematic literature review informed by an expert panel, not a primary RCT. It reviews 116 articles but is not itself an RCT.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled maintenance trial with 130 older adults aged 65+ with recently remitted major depression. Randomized to maintenance antidepressant pharmacotherapy with donepezil or placebo. Meets all criteria: elderly, remitted from depression, randomized to maintenance treatment.

This is about recruitment strategies for a dietary intervention trial exploring diet and immune function, not depression treatment. Does not meet the intervention criteria (not about antidepressants or psychological therapies for depression maintenance).

This is a 2x2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with patients older than 59 years (average age 67). 107 patients fully recovered after acute treatment were randomly assigned to 4 maintenance therapy conditions (nortriptyline, IPT, both, or placebo). Meets all criteria: elderly, recovered from depression, randomized to maintenance treatment.
This is a methodology paper describing a rating scale for depression, not an RCT. No intervention or randomization involved.

While this is an RCT with elderly people (65+) with depression, it tests acute treatment effectiveness (CBT vs TAU vs talking control) rather than continuation/maintenance treatment after successful treatment. The objective is to determine clinical effectiveness of CBT for older people WITH depression, not for preventing relapse/recurrence after remission.
This is a methodology paper describing development of a therapy rating scale to discriminate between maintenance treatments. Not an RCT testing treatment efficacy.
